answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate pressure on price-sensitive SMB, but memory_73 and exp_73 show targeted discounting backfires on retention and renewal—it attracts cohorts that churn at renewal, destroying long-term qualified revenue. This is precisely the wrong direction when sustainable revenue is the primary objective. Instead, memory_44 and exp_31 show that enterprise sales-assist (demo-request paths) and onboarding simplification both drive durable value. The current churn pressure on SMBs should be redirected: (1) protect the SMB base by investing in completion velocity and activation (memory_86, memory_91) to improve their early product success and stickiness, and (2) concurrently launch a sales-assist flow targeting the mid-market and enterprise segments where competitive discounting is less relevant and conversion quality is higher. This preserves margins, builds sustainable pipeline, and avoids the retention trap of promotional pricing. A standard experiment on enterprise sales-assist routes allows real-time optimization while protecting the SMB base from a discount spiral. The uncertainty of which SMB subsets can be saved vs. will churn regardless is preserved; we are not assuming discounting will solve retention.
